title: Prime gap limit points for normalized gaps

problemStatement.plain: Erdos #5 asks whether every non-negative real number, together with infinity, occurs as a limit point of normalized prime gaps (p_{n+1}-p_n)/log(n). The Lean file defines the normalized gap sequence, proves basic structural facts about its limit-point set, and packages known deep prime-gap inputs as axioms.
whyMatters: Connects prime-gap distribution to a clean topological statement about subsequential limits.
Separates elementary consequences of prime ordering from deep inputs such as bounded gaps and large-gap theorems.

proven: `nthPrime`, `primeGap`, `normalizedGap`, `IsLimitPoint`, and `limitPointSet` define the normalized prime-gap setting.
`zhang_implies_zero_limit`, `zero_mem_limitPointSet`, and `goldston_pintz_yildirim_small_gaps` derive 0 as a limit point from bounded-gaps input.
`westzynthius_implies_frequently_large` and `frequently_normalizedGap_gt` capture arbitrarily large normalized gaps from Westzynthius input.
`limitPointSet_isClosed`, `erdos_5_iff`, `erdos_5_from_dense_values`, and `erdos_5_iff_dense_at_every_point` reframe the conjecture as set equality and frequent-neighborhood density.
open: `erdos_5` remains open: proving every non-negative real is a limit point is the main missing theorem.
`westzynthius_large_gaps`, `zhang_bounded_gaps`, and `hildebrand_maier_large_limit_points` are axioms for deep external number-theory results.
Measure-theoretic results about the size of the limit-point set are noted but not formalized here.
knownResults.goal: Keep the topological limit-point reductions theorem-backed while replacing deep prime-gap axioms only when the required analytic number theory is available.
